summary: Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Julius Jolly (~1911–1914) and served as Professor of Iranian Studies at Deccan College (~1939–1942) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1956).

Irawati Karve worked in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied at Fergusson College, Huzurpaga, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. She served at Deccan College as Professor of Sociology and Anthropology (~1939–1970) and at the University of Pennsylvania (~1951–1952).

Irfan Habib is a historian working in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (1947–1953), and New College (1954–1958). In ~1953, he took up a post as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University.

Irina Anatolyevna Svetovidova was an Indologist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1950–1955). She served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (1957–1968) and taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1965–1968).

Irving Babbitt was a philosopher. He studied at Harvard, Williams College, the University of Paris, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He taught Romance languages at Williams College (1893–1894) and was an assistant professor at Harvard University (1894–1912).

Isaac Schapera worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and under Bronisław Malinowski at the London School of Economics (~1926–1929). He held posts at Chicago (~1948–1949), the London School of Economics (~1950–1969), and Toronto (~1953–1954).

Isaak Jakob Schmidt worked in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Holding a doctorate from Rostock, he served at the Russian Bible Society (~1812–1826), Saint Petersburg State University (~1827–1847), and the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1829–1847).

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy works in Tibetology. She studied at ULB, Tibet University, EPHE under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert, Harvard, and Qinghai Nationalities University. In 2007, she became a Full Professor at Laval University.

Isabelle Onians is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 2002 and served as an editor for the Clay Sanskrit Library, attested in 2007.

Isabelle Ratié specializes in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Paris 1, EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon, and under Alexis Sanderson. Her posts include Leipzig (~2010–2013), Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and professor at the Collège de France (2025).

Isaiah Berlin was a scholar in philosophy and history and archaeology. He was educated at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1928–1932), and held an academic post at the University of Oxford from ~1932 to 1997.

Isaline Blew Horner worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Cambridge and under Caroline Rhys Davids, she served at Newnham College (1918–1936), the University of Cambridge governing body (1939–1949), and as Hon. Secretary of the Pali Text Society (1942–1981).
Isamu Kanaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 1976, he held posts as a professor at both Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College.

Isao Nishitani works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held a post at Sennyu-ji (attested 2016) and serves as an associate professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).

Iselin Frydenlund is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. Attested in 2016, she held posts as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and as a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. Educated at Sanskrit College and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, he served as a teacher and head clerk at Fort William College (1841–1849) and as director at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1851).

Isidor Isaac Scheftelowitz worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Königsberg under Adalbert Bezzenberger (1897–1901), later serving at the University of Cologne (1919–1933) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1933–1934).

Ismael Quiles Sánchez was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Colegio Máximo de San Ignacio and San José, he served as Vice-Rector (1956–1962) and Prorector (1965–1974) at Universidad del Salvador, and visited Georgetown University (1950–1965).

Iso Kern is a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at KU Leuven, Freiburg, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University. He held academic posts at KU Leuven (1962–1971), Heidelberg (~1973–1979), and the University of Bern (1985).
Issaien Ikeyama is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Shitennoji Junior College and at Eizan Gakuin, both attested in 1976.
